title: Continuum presents an exhibit for Miami Art Week by Avant Gallery and Rebecca Setareh
summary: Continuum, South Florida’s premier resort-style oceanfront condominium residences in Miami Beach, continues its collaboration with today’s leading galleries and artists, as part of its world-class series of art programming taking place annually during Miami Art Week. Presenting a premier collection of works by today’s leaders in modern and contemporary art, Continuum has formed an exclusive partnership with Miami’s acclaimed Avant Gallery to showcase a total of 21 hand-picked pieces of art, curated by the gallery’s founder, Dmitry Prut. Beginning on November 30th this year and running until February 12th 2027, a signature exhibit by some of today’s world-renowned artists will be shown within the lobby areas of both Continuum North and South towers. title: Peggy Guggenheim Collection presents Fucina degli Angeli Murano glass retrospective
summary: From November 14, 2026, through March 29, 2027, the Peggy Guggenheim Collection presents Fucina degli Angeli: Peggy Guggenheim and 20th-century Artistic Glass, a comprehensive exhibition that sheds light on one of the most visionary chapters of postwar Murano glass through an in-depth historical analysis of the experiments, collaborations, and relationships that left a mark on the history of twentieth-century art. Organized by Cristina Beltrami, the show traces the creative adventure of the Fucina degli Angeli, founded by Egidio Costantini in the mid-1950s. Peggy Guggenheim’s role is central to this story: she supported Costantini at crucial moments and contributed to the international success of the project—not only by acquiring numerous pieces for her collection, also by broadening Costantini's network to include leading figures in twentieth-century art and proposing an exhibition strategy that benefitted from her extensive experience as a

title: Christie's New York to auction Ted Turner's American West art collection
summary: When the visionary media mogul Ted Turner was asked about his plans for his Montana ranch, he used to say, “I want my lands to look and feel like those,” gesturing to the paintings on his living room walls – awe-inspiring panoramas of the American West in its untouched state by the preeminent landscape artists Albert Bierstadt (1830-1902) and Thomas Moran (1837-1926). On January 20, 2027, Christie's New York will hold a special live evening auction: Trailblazer: Ted Turner's America, presenting approximately 20 exceptional works by Bierstadt and Moran from the private collection of Ted Turner. The top lot is Bierstadt's masterpiece Yosemite Valley (estimate: $4,000,000-6,000,000), which maintained pride of place above the mantle at Turner's famed Flying D Ranch in Montana. title: Norton Simon Museum presents Édouard Manet's 'The Execution of Maximilian'
summary: The Norton Simon Museum presents Making History: Manet’s “Execution of Maximilian” from the National Gallery, London. On view from November 13, 2026, through March 1, 2027, the exhibition is centered on Édouard Manet’s The Execution of Maximilian (c. 1867–68), one of the French artist’s most ambitious paintings, made all the more compelling by its now-fragmentary condition. The second of five versions (four paintings and one print) that Manet created, this monumental work depicts the death by firing squad of Austrian archduke Ferdinand Maximilian, the short-lived emperor of Mexico, at the hands of forces loyal to ousted Mexican president Benito Juárez in 1867. The execution—along with that of his generals Tomás Mejía and Miguel Miramón—shocked Europe, where many, including Manet, blamed French emperor Napoleon III, who had enticed Maximilian to take the throne. title: Fondation Beyeler's 2027 exhibition programme: Frida Kahlo, Louise Bourgeois and Elizabeth Peyton
summary: Celebrating the expansion of its ensemble throughout 2027, the Fondation Beyelerʼs exhibition programme brings together three major solo exhibitions dedicated to influential artists of the 20th and 21st centuries: Frida Kahlo, Louise Bourgeois and Elizabeth Peyton. These exhibitions take place alongside the inaugural exhibition “Constellations", which is already unfolding across the expanded ensemble. Early in the new year, the Fondation Beyeler will devote a major retrospective to Frida Kahlo (1907–1954). Featuring over 50 paintings, the exhibition will bring together approximately one third of her entire painted oeuvre. It will further present 15 characteristic works on paper. As the first monographic exhibition of Frida Kahlo in Switzerland, the retrospective offers both a comprehensive overview of the artistʼs work and a unique insight into an oeuvre that is rarely seen in Europe. title: A monumental Lee Bul exhibition occupies two floors at M HKA
summary: On November 13, M HKA will open Lee Bul: From 1998 to Now, the artist’s most comprehensive survey to date. Lee Bul is a key figure in contemporary art, with an internationally recognised practice. Featuring major installations — including Willing To Be Vulnerable — Metalized Balloon (2019), a ten-metre-long zeppelin — the exhibition unfolds across two floors of the museum, a first for a solo exhibition at M HKA. Tracing key developments in her practice from the late 1990s to today, the exhibition brings together more than 150 works, ranging from drawings, maquettes and two-dimensional works to sculptures and monumental installations. Across this diverse body of work, Lee Bul explores modernist and utopian visions of the future, architecture and the historical avant-garde. title: Kunsthalle Mannheim explores 150 years of dance in visual art
summary: How can an ephemeral moment become art when it vanishes almost as soon as it comes into being? This is the central tension explored in DANCE!, a new exhibition opening at the Kunsthalle Mannheim on November 13. Covering more than 150 years, the exhibition explores how visual artists have drawn inspiration from the ever-changing movements of dance, using them as a starting point for new forms of artistic expression. Conceived by Johan Holten, the Kunsthalle’s former director – who was once a dancer at the Hamburg State Opera– the exhibition explores the dynamic interplay between visual art and choreography. It reveals how artists from the modernist era to the present day have continually reinterpreted the dancing body as an expression of freedom, identity and social change. title: Aguttes to auction original 1989 portrait of Michael Jackson
summary: On 26 January 1990, at the Beverly Hilton in Los Angeles, Michael Jackson stood beside his own portrait. Entitled The Book, the painting by Brett-Livingstone Strong depicts the singer dressed in red velvet, holding a closed book in his hands. Its acquisition, reportedly valued at $2.1 million as part of an agreement that also included commercial exploitation rights, made international headlines. At the time, the painting was described in the press as the most expensive portrait of a living person. More than three decades after that unveiling, Aguttes will offer the original painting at auction. Michael Jackson beyond the stage: Completed in December 1989, following the worldwide success of Bad, The Book grew out of the friendship and artistic collaboration between Jackson and Strong. According to accounts from those close to the singer, it is believed to be the only painted portrait for which Jackson personally sat.

title: Smithsonian-led scientists anchor first scientific animal name to a modern-day spider
summary: Scientists led by the Smithsonian’s National Museum of Natural History have restored the physical reference of one of the most historically significant names in biology. In a paper published today in Taxonomy, researchers designated a new type specimen, or neotype, for Araneus angulatus, the first animal species described using binomial nomenclature, the two-part naming system that scientists use today to identify and classify living organisms. The designation reconnects the name to a physical specimen decades after the original name-bearing spiders disappeared. The button-size spider Araneus angulatus was originally described in 1757 by Swedish arachnologist Carl Alexander Clerck. To support his description, Clerck preserved three A. angulatus spiders that served as “types,” specimens that define what a species name refers to. title: National Museum of Scotland opens major exhibition on Roman occupation
summary: Opening this weekend, a major exhibition at the National Museum of Scotland sheds new light on the Roman occupation in Scotland, demonstrating how this significant frontier was supplied from across the Empire, and looking at the impacts this occupation had on the local population. Bringing together recent research, significant loans from across Europe and previously unseen archaeological discoveries from Scotland, Roman Scotland: Life on the Edge of Empire tells new stories of Roman occupation and reshapes our understanding of Scotland’s relationship with the Roman world. Central to the exhibition are finds from a 2nd century AD Roman fort at Inveresk in East Lothian, a site whose full significance is revealed in this exhibition. title: Cincinnati Art Museum names inaugural Mary W. Baskett Curator of Fashion Arts and Textiles
summary: The Cincinnati Art Museum has named David E. (Ned) Lazaro the inaugural Mary W. Baskett Curator of Fashion Arts and Textiles. Lazaro will be responsible for the stewardship, growth, development and programmatic initiatives of the museum’s fashion and textiles collection. He will begin December 1, 2026. “We are pleased to welcome Ned Lazaro to Cincinnati,” shared Cameron Kitchin, Louis and Louise Dieterle Nippert Director of the Cincinnati Art Museum. “His leadership and voice in fashion and textile studies will benefit our entire community, building on generational commitments at the Cincinnati Art Museum. We look forward to Ned’s contributions and collaborative scholarship at CAM." Lazaro joins CAM from The Wadsworth (Hartford, Connecticut) where he oversaw the museum’s global costume and textile collection of more than 10,000 works, ranging in date from ancient to contemporary as the Associate Curator of Costume and Textiles. title: Alisan Fine Arts presents Li Hongwei's first New York solo exhibition
summary: Alisan Fine Arts presents Finding the Balance, Li Hongwei’s first New York City solo exhibition, on view from November 13th, 2026 through December 23rd, 2026. Based between Princeton, NJ and Beijing, China, Li is a unique artistic voice within the Chinese diaspora. He has taken the production of Chinese porcelain and metalwork into his own hands, harnessing these mediums to create his own contemporary vocabulary. In 2005, Li Hongwei left China to study ceramic art at the New York State College of Ceramics (Alfred University), receiving his MFA in 2007 and continuing to teach in New York for several years. At the same time, Li embarked on a remarkable exploration of ancient Chinese ceramics, and he began to fuse porcelain with contemporary materials, developing the various series of artworks on view in the current exhibition. title: Hauser & Wirth New York presents Harmony Korine's debut solo exhibition
summary: Harmony Korine has developed a wide-ranging practice over the last three decades that spans film, painting, sculpture and fashion, all unified by a distinctive combination of improvisation, humor, repetition, nostalgia and poetry. Moving freely between mediums, Korine continually invents imaginative new visual languages that resist easy categorization. Across his varied oeuvre, each body of work unfolds with its own formal and emotional lexicon. This November, Korine carries his genre-defying worldbuilding into new territory with 'UX LAM' an exhibition of new paintings for his debut with Hauser & Wirth New York. This presentation follows 'Harmony Korine: Perfect Nonsense,' the artist's first US museum survey, presented by the Institute of Contemporary Art, Miami, in 2026. title: Archives of American Art announces new craft exhibition and launches monthly podcast
summary: The Smithsonian’s Archives of American Art announced today “Materials, Methods, and Meanings: Craft in the Archives of American Art,” a new exhibition exploring stories of craft that have shaped the American experience. Now on view at the Lawrence A. Fleischman Gallery in the Donald W. Reynolds Center for American Art and Portraiture in Washington, D.C., the exhibition is a contribution to the Smithsonian's celebration of the United States’ 250th anniversary. The Archives also announced the launch of United States of Craft, a new monthly podcast. Hosted by Glenn Adamson and Sarah Archer, the series will bring to listeners the voices and stories of makers, thinkers and visionaries shaping craft across the nation. title: Lorna Simpson to receive the 2027 Wolfgang Hahn Prize
summary: American artist Lorna Simpson (*1960, lives and works in Brooklyn, New York) will receive the 33rd Wolfgang Hahn Prize in 2027, awarded by the Gesellschaft für Moderne Kunst at the Museum Ludwig. The joint decision was made by the jury, comprising of Naomi Beckwith, Deputy Director and Chief Curator of the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum in New York and Artistic Director of documenta 16 and the board of the Gesellschaft für Moderne Kunst. The prize includes, as always, the acquisition of a work by the award recipient for the collection of the Museum Ludwig. Lorna Simpson is regarded as a pioneering American conceptual artist. Her multifaceted body of work will provide, in the jury’s view, an important impetus for the Museum Ludwig’s collection of American art. title: Historic $5M gift expands Asian art wing at Phoenix Art Museum
summary: Phoenix Art Museum announced a historic gift from Arizona-based philanthropist, physician, and biotechnology executive Sukumar Nagendran that establishes PhxArt as a leading U.S. art museum with a dedicated Sri Lankan art initiative. The gift creates the Nagendran Gallery for the Art of Sri Lanka and South Asia, dedicates the Dr. Sukumar Nagendran Wing for the Art of Asia, and provides ongoing support for acquisitions and exhibitions, scholarly research, and public programs designed to elevate South Asian artistic voices. The significant $5M gift also expands the institution’s dedicated Art of Asia galleries to more than 9,500 sq. ft. and deepens its commitment to the presentation and preservation of Asian art, one of the Museum’s foundational collections. title: Frankfurter Kunstverein examines digital propaganda and online subcultures in new exhibition
summary: Propaganda in the “post-truth” era is noisy, fast and emotional. Images, memes and codes create a sense of belonging and convey political convictions, often before these become recognisable. Communication strategies in online communities dominate political spheres and have heavily impacted the public debate. Curated by the Frankfurter Kunstverein, the exhibition Propaganda – Flooding the Zone with Shit – It’s About Money, Stupid! examines how propaganda operates under these current conditions, how political convictions take shape and which economic interests influence their dissemination. The seven invited artists have worked intensively on propaganda and online subcultures for years. They gained sharp insight into political affiliations, how emotions are mobilised and how power becomes embedded in technologies

title: Major exhibition traces Ragtime's journey from Black American roots to the mainstream
summary: The Morgan Library & Museum presents Ragtime: Cakewalk in Pianoland, an exhibition introducing visitors to one of the first truly global popular-music styles. On view from November 13, 2026, through June 13, 2027, the exhibition follows ragtime's path, from the musical traditions of enslaved Black people to the parlors and saloons of rising industrial centers in nineteenth-century America, and on to the nightclubs and concert halls of the world. Along the way, the exhibition tells a story fundamental to American culture, one that connects ragtime to jazz, rock, and hip-hop: how Black cultural traditions and creativity have continually shaped, influenced, and been adapted within American music and art. title: Sara-Vide Ericson debuts sixty Arctic-inspired artworks at Stockholm's Liljevalchs
summary: DRIFT begins in the Arctic Ocean, on board the icebreaker Oden, embarking on both an inner and outer expedition. Over six weeks, Sara-Vide Ericson works in a container on deck painting sixty new works, while the ship is breaking through two-metre-thick ice surrounded by a landscape that’s constantly shifting. In 2025, Sara-Vide joins the expedition Canada-Sweden Arctic Ocean in which the icebreaker Oden paves the way through the frozen landscape. The process is both transformative and strenuous, including helicopter excursions onto the ice to gather material for the works emerging on board as well as for the continued work in the artist’s home studio in Hälsingland. title: Group exhibition at Van Abbehuis explores wrestling, spectacle, and political staging
summary: For Piledriver, scores of practices are brought together that consider the exhibition an arena. Within its capacity as an ideologically vacuous zone, the actuality of the staged space colludes in adaptive political stances. Anna-Sophie Berger, Oroma Elewa, Julie Falk, Harun Farocki, Lourdes Grobet, Runo Lagomarsino, Twan Lugten, Céline Mathieu, Jacqueline Mesmaeker, Jonathan Monk and Gozié Ojini do not resolve into a fixed position. Kayfabe and spectatorship are kept in the same hold; the crowd enters the square called a ring. Wrestling is the longest standing excuse for an oiled-up pair to clasp in public. From the Greek palaestra to Turkish yağlı güreş, where olive-drenched pehlivans reach for grip onto the rivals leather shorts, intimacy is continually staged as combat. title: 125 Newbury presents new paintings and drawings by artist Asher Liftin
summary: 125 Newbury presents Asher Liftin: Recent Work, an exhibition of new paintings and drawings by the Brooklyn-based artist on view from September 18 through November 7 at 395 Broadway in Tribeca. Following Liftin’s Summer 2026 Artist Residency at The Watermill Center in Watermill, New York, the exhibition is curated by Arne Glimcher and accompanied by a written introduction by Glimcher in the gallery’s 125 Free Press publication. Asher Liftin’s work investigates fundamental conditions of vision and visibility. Using his own photography as source material, he translates mechanical images refracted in a glass eye into meticulously hand-crafted renderings on canvas and paper. The resulting images both evoke and extend histories of pointillism and divisionism, summoning the tradition of painters from Paul Signac to Chuck Close. As

title: Gertrude Abercrombie and Andy Warhol lead Rago Wright's $3.8M art sales
summary: Rago Wright's November 11 presentations of Post War & Contemporary Art and Pop Insider: The Collection of the Artist Idelle Weber together realized more than $3.8 million in sales, drawing enthusiastic bidding for important examples of 20th- and 21st-century art. Post War & Contemporary Art achieved a sale total of $3,368,040, selling 120% by value, while Pop Insider: The Collection of the Artist Idelle Weber realized $463,333, selling 126% by value. Leading Post War & Contemporary Art was Gertrude Abercrombie's extraordinary 1956 oil painting Two Shells, Lady (Figure) on Beach, which achieved $281,600, nearly doubling its $150,000 high estimate. title: Kunsthalle Wien presents Tiffany Sia's first Austrian institutional solo exhibition
summary: Kunsthalle Wien presents the first institutional solo exhibition in Austria by Tiffany Sia (b. 1988, Hong Kong). Curated by Carina Bukuts, Overt Listening brings together footage from the artist’s first feature length film, shot across Taiwan’s Kinmen Islands, with a series of newly commissioned video works and sculptures. Unfolding across the ground floor of Kunsthalle Wien’s Museumsquartier building and the Studio on Level−1, the exhibition examines how histories of conflict are made public, circulated and withheld through the cameras, broadcasts and military infrastructure that govern what can be seen and heard. An artist, filmmaker and writer, Sia advances arguments through form, commenting on the relationship between media, political power and collective memory.
